title: Fine Gardening (Paul Zimmerman) — When to Prune a Young Rose

common.applies_to: Bush rose; recently planted / restraint period
common.preserved_uncertainty: Commercial gardening publication, not an institutional source — lower reliability tier than the extension sources also cited for AF-1.
mil_references: ARC-BUSHROSE-RECENTPLANT-01, AF-1 (Moderate) — restraint period for full pruning

content.source_type: Recognised horticultural publication (commercial; named, experienced rosarian author)
content.identity: Fine Gardening, Paul Zimmerman, "When to Prune a Young Rose," https://www.finegardening.com/project-guides/pruning/how-soon-can-you-prune-a-young-rose, accessed during FRD-BUSHROSE-RECENTPLANT-01 research
content.relevance: States a young rose (planted the previous year) should not be pruned; original nursery canes typically replaced "by the third year or so." Independently converges with the Illinois Extension threshold.
